entries.label: Semicolon separator (id)
entries.notes: Semicolon ends the intended command and runs id; benign output proves execution on Unix shells.

entries.label: Pipe into command
entries.notes: Pipes the first command's output into id; fires regardless of the first command's exit status.

entries.label: Conditional AND (&&)
entries.notes: Runs id only when the preceding command succeeds; survives inputs that must stay syntactically valid.

entries.label: Conditional OR (||)
entries.notes: Runs id when the preceding command fails; useful when tampered input makes the legitimate command error.

entries.label: Background/chain ampersand
entries.notes: On cmd.exe a single ampersand chains unconditionally; on Unix it backgrounds the first command so both still run — handy for blind injection where the original must not block.

entries.label: Encoded newline separator
entries.notes: URL-encoded line feed injects a fresh command line where the shell splits on newlines.

entries.label: Command substitution $()
entries.notes: POSIX substitution executes inline and embeds output in the surrounding argument; nests cleanly.

entries.label: Backtick substitution
entries.notes: Legacy backtick substitution; fallback when $() is filtered.

entries.label: Blind time delay (sleep)
entries.notes: No output channel required: a measurable five-second delay confirms blind injection on Unix.

entries.label: Blind delay via ping (Windows)
entries.notes: Ping count introduces a timed delay on Windows where command output is not reflected.

entries.label: Out-of-band DNS exfil
entries.notes: Resolves a subdomain carrying command output; observable on a controlled nameserver when no in-band channel exists.

entries.label: Out-of-band HTTP callback
entries.notes: Sends base64 output over HTTP; works when DNS is filtered but outbound HTTP is allowed.

entries.label: Space bypass with ${IFS}
entries.notes: ${IFS} expands to whitespace, defeating filters that block literal spaces.

entries.label: Space bypass with brace expansion
entries.notes: Brace expansion passes arguments without spaces; slips past naive space blocklists.

entries.label: Break quoted argument
entries.notes: Closes a single-quoted shell argument, injects id, then reopens the quote to keep syntax valid.

entries.label: Windows chain (whoami)
entries.notes: cmd.exe command chaining; whoami is a side-effect-free execution proof on Windows.

entries.label: PowerShell statement separator
entries.notes: Semicolon separates PowerShell statements; Get-Process proves execution without changes.

entries.label: Argument injection (output flag)
entries.notes: When input becomes argv to a tool like curl/wget, inject flags rather than shell metacharacters.

entries.label: Keyword split via quotes
entries.notes: Empty-string concatenation breaks the keyword for signature WAFs; the shell reassembles cat.

entries.label: Glob the binary name
entries.notes: Single-character glob matches /bin/cat, evading literal cat filters.
